title: Kinetic² solver scratch is thread_local (10 KB of TLS): every FreeRTOS task must host it in its stack, the IPC task has 1 KB, the P4 asserts in esp_ipc_init and boot-loops
description: Found on the bench 2026-10-06 flashing Nucleus 0.1.16 (the first Kinetic²-only image): assert in esp_ipc_init (xTaskCreatePinnedToCore of ipc0) before app_main, rebooting every ~1.4 s. jerk::solve keeps its banded matrix as static thread_local (solver.hpp ~220, A[kMaxUnknowns][2*kHalfBand+1] + b), so the image carries a 10,240 B .tbss; ESP-IDF places each task's TLS block inside the task's own stack, so a task whose stack is smaller than the TLS cannot be created. title: Kinetic² renderer is the handle model: a composite cubic Bézier per span, G1/G2 by knot class, handle lengths bounded by the ceilings, amplitude trimmed toward the previous knot; replaces the spend ladder
description: Operator ruling 2026-10-07, 'this is K2'. The renderer between knots becomes the handle model proven in playground/handles.html (kin-d0o; handles-model.js is the reference implementation and the acceptance: the kernel matches it on the 1 ms grid for the built-in script within float tolerance). The five cases: (1) classify each knot from its chords: hold edge (zero chord on a side), crest (sign change), through point (same sign), ends at rest; (2) the angle by style: zero at crests and hold edges, PCHIP's monotone rule or Makima's at a through point, G2 solving the through angle in closed form (both sides linear in it), held to the Fritsch-Carlson band and vmax; (3) handle lengths a third of each span (exact PCHIP); the smooth style matches a crest's two lengths by their ratio for G2; (4) the ceilings scale a piece's two lengths by one factor, nearest one, never under the feel floor (handle_floor, default 0.15); speed caps from above, acceleration and jerk from below, the window is a ceiling; (5) amplitude: when no length is legal the later knot moves toward the previous knot's actual position by the least that is legal (bisection), a reachable knot never moves, a hold after a trimmed knot moves with it, angles re-solve from the trimmed chords; time never, the lateness budget defaults to zero. On top: the corner ramp |da|/jmax at a G1 knot, the tightest legal rounding at a G0 knot. Replaces in solver.hpp and profile.hpp: the corner attempt loop, SATURATE/DILATE/TRIM, the lateness budget and absorbable placement (RFC-105 (aaa), (bbb)). Unchanged: the knot timeline, the horizon and lookahead, supersede, re-plan from the live state, the sampler, the ABI. Acceptance beyond parity: the three suites green with a fingerprint changed on purpose; the lab's scripts no worse than c3af1ed inside the ceilings (conditional_dnp 0.48 mm mean, Krampus at 200 mm 3.2, the 20 s sine 1.2, the tongue 2.4) and the sawtooth rendered on time with its rise trimmed per the ruling; the wasm twin and the lab follow; RFC-106 carries the wire side (curve_families pchip and smooth), RFC-105's anticipated-workflow log gets the (ccc) entry. Known cost (RFC-106 Cons): one cubic per span needs about twice an S-curve's acceleration at the same peak speed, so over-ceiling spans trim more than saturate did; machine-inserted cruise pieces are the extension if the motor asks.

title: Dense reversals at 33 ms spans are beyond any cubic rendering: a 30 Hz burst needs the chain's sinusoid
description: Measured in the Kinetic² lab 2026-10-07 on ApracticedtongueDLV at a 100 mm window (vmax 1000, amax 50000, jmax 5e6): the 30 Hz sections (10 mm reversals every 33 ms, PCHIP, C1) trim to the floor and stretch 30 to 70 ms per knot, before and after the cubic spends (kin-g5u): mean error 2.3 mm before, 3.0 after, with the first burst lagging past 120 ms and two knots dropped; the rest of the script (66 to 133 ms spans with end velocities) renders exact. Why: a PCHIP reversal flips the acceleration from +55k to -55k mm/s^2 at every knot, and Corner::Cubic joins the two cubics with a jerk-limited ramp of 110k / 5e6 = 22 ms, inside a 33 ms span: the head keeps 11 ms for a cubic that needs 33, so no dilation fits and the knot falls to the smooth path, where a rest-to-rest quintic over 33 ms is jerk-bound three times over (60 d / T^3) and trims. The author's curve has infinite jerk at every knot; no rendering keeps its shape. A 15 Hz sinusoid of 10 mm p-p is feasible at jmax 5e6 (jerk 4.2e6) with the whole amplitude: the minimum-jerk chain through the reversals CAN render it, if the junction accelerations anticipate the next reversal (a sinusoid peaks in acceleration at its reversals, +-44k) instead of being solved one piece at a time from a pinned start state. Asked: when the corner ramp would eat more than half a span, render the run of such knots as the chain's smooth curve with free junction accelerations solved jointly over the lookahead (the sinusoid), at full amplitude, and report nothing; the operator's K1 memory of dense scripts ('struggled but kept it uniform') is this. Reproduce: the lab, the tongue recording, zoom 11.3 to 13.2 s; or a built-in pattern 33:10,33:0 at a 100 mm window.
notes:
Operator ruling 2026-10-07 (RFC-103 amendment): the oscillator is an additional feature; a script's rapid vibration on the main axis must still render as well as the planner can, nothing routes it to the oscillator. So this bead stays a renderer concern under the handle model (kin-y6e): a 30 Hz burst of 33 ms spans is a run of crests at the jerk and acceleration ceilings; the handle lengths floor and the trim toward the previous knot give the reachable amplitude, which the lab must measure against the tongue script once kin-y6e lands.
Measured on handles-model.js 2026-10-07, a train of 12 reversals, 60 mm asked, hold edges either side: at 33 ms spans the renderer reaches 11.0 mm of stroke (amax 50000, jmax 5e6), 12.3 (jmax 2e7), 15.0 (amax 100000), 20.9 (amax 100000, jmax 2e7); at 50 ms spans 28.3 / 28.3 / 33.4 / 34.2. Handle lengths come out 0.37 to 0.42 (flat crests, a fast middle), the crests G2 by symmetry with no corner ramp inside the train, nothing infeasible. A sinusoid of the same half-period reaches 11 mm at amax 50000 and bang-bang 13.6, so the cubic train sits at the physical limit: the title's claim that a burst needs the chain's sinusoid does not hold under the handle model; the motor's acceleration ceiling is the only limit, and it scales linearly. Retitle when kin-y6e lands and the lab measures the tongue script.
Operator ruling 2026-10-08: samples (0x2100) carry position only. The hub holds one or two samples for lookahead and renders a minimum-jerk bang-bang move to the destination (Profile::point from the live state toward the newest held sample, re-planned as each sample lands, never trimmed, never a Bezier); segments (0x2101) alone get the handle renderer. Resolves the dense-sample cost (12.9 ms per sample on the P4) and this bead's 33 ms reversals: a point profile has no corner to fit.

Defaults, authored ahead, flags 0. reset(0.1, 0); one C1 knot v=0 at (600 ms, 0.5). Samples: 1..~274 ms p 0.331056 v 2.40857 a 0 held constant (dp/dt 0 while v reads 2.41); at 275 ms p is back near 0.1 and the real motion runs, landing at 0.5 at 600 ms at rest. The minimum position no longer winds up below the start (kin-f1t item 1 fixed), but the state before the head starts is wrong: a 0.231 position step at 1 ms and another back at 275 ms. Staircase (five C1 v=0 steps from 0.1 every 300 ms) shows the same at every step (1 ms: p 0.186 v 1.269; 300 ms: p 0.336 v 1.269, dp/dt 86). Looks like Piece::at() for t before the hard head's start returns a clamped or extrapolated head state instead of the hold. Also: solver.hpp uses std::max without #include <algorithm>; the emscripten build (cmake --build build-wasm --target kinetic2_wasm) fails with 4 errors at solver.hpp:398, 584, 591.
notes: Cause: Piece::at computed tau from an unsigned difference, so a time before the piece's start wrapped and returned the END state; a hard-stop head from rest (which now starts later than the origin) showed its launch state for the whole hold. Fixed: before its start a piece holds its start state. <algorithm> included in solver.hpp. check.mjs staircase and hardstop pass with the real module.
close_reason: Piece::at hold-before-start fixed; algorithm include added; presets green.

title: Kinetic² streamed submits teleport the carriage: a stretched knot re-solves at the re-plan origin in zero time (position step up to 0.1 window, jerk 20x jmax)
description:
Found by the playground (kin-8ef), reproduced in bare node against build-wasm/wasm/kinetic2.wasm with no solved() reads (no observer effect). Defaults (vmax 3, amax 30, jmax 500, Blend, floor 0.25, react 4 ms, lookahead 250 ms). reset(0.2, 0); every 100 ms from now=0 submit a free C2 knot 100 ms ahead (t=100..500 ms, p=0.3..0.7); sample at 1 ms.
Trace: submit@0 knot(100,0.3) solves to t 244.4 ms, share 0.25, stretched 144 ms. submit@100 knot(200,0.4): the pending window shows the first knot at t 104 ms (= now + react) p 0.2097 v 0 a 0. Samples: 100 ms p 0.1809 v -0.332; 104 ms p 0.2097 v 0 (p step +0.030). Same at 204 ms (+0.054) and 404 ms (+0.099, from v -0.807 to 0). Knots after the step are reported DeadlineStretched 8.000 s (the cap) then PlanFailed detail 1e30 (kIllegal) and dropped.
Reading: in submit() the re-plan commits the curve to tr and sets origin = piece.at(tr), but the re-solve places the still-pending stretched knot at its authored time (100 ms, now behind the origin) clamped to the origin, so the piece to it has zero duration and the origin jumps to the knot's state. Its earlier stretch is forgotten on re-solve.
Also seen: 60 Hz streamed 1 Hz sine (amplitude 0.35, well inside every ceiling) at 16 ms latency: p step 0.152 -> 0.115 at 305 ms, |j| 10961 vs jmax 500, 830 anomalies over 60 knots. Ahead-authored versions of the same knots have no steps and stay under jmax. Playground presets Scrub and Starved stream show it; playground/check.mjs lists them as expected failures citing this bead.
notes: Fixed 2026-10-06 in the kernel (uncommitted at the time of this note, see the commit that references this id): samples persist their solved time and junction across re-solves (Prior), the first sample keeps the committed curve, new samples sit at an eased 0.9x spacing so the lag closes at the tail, interior samples take min-jerk junctions. Playground scrub and starved presets pass check.mjs with the real module.

title: Handles playground: a funscript as a composite cubic Bezier in the time-position plane, knot classes G0/G1/G2 per knot, draggable handles, the ceilings as bounds on the handle lengths, a tolerance box for the nudges
description: A second static page beside the Kinetic2 playground (playground/handles.html, handles.js, handles-model.js) for the handle model under study (the 2026-10-07 design conversation): the script's knots stay on the author's clock, each knot has one angle (velocity) and two handle lengths (time influence, fractions of the adjacent spans; a third is the exact PCHIP cubic), G0 marks a corner with two angles, G1 one angle with free lengths, G2 acceleration continuity (angle for a through point, lengths for a crest), auto classifies from the chords (hold edge, crest, through). The ceilings bound the lengths per piece (speed from above, acceleration and jerk from below); a piece that no length satisfies may move its knot within a tolerance box; what remains is shown as infeasible. The page loads a .funscript, lets the operator set each knot's class and drag its handles (aligned, Blender style), and shows velocity, acceleration and jerk against the ceilings with every nudge visible. Pure JS model, no wasm: this is the design playground, not the kernel. handles.check.mjs runs the model on the built-in script and asserts the figure numbers (a 150 mm / 200 ms stroke between crests fits at a length of 0.25 under 1000 mm/s and 50000 mm/s2) and, with Playwright available, that the page loads with zero console errors.
notes:
Operator rulings 2026-10-07. (1) Through points are G2 by default, crests and hold edges stay G1 (PCHIP as drawn, the corner ramp takes the step); a Makima/Akima-style request makes every knot G2: the style select (pchip | smooth), hold edges flat in both, the window is a ceiling, the inspector shows handle lengths in ms. (2) Amplitude: when no handle length is legal, the later knot moves toward the previous knot's actual position by the least that is legal (bisection; time kept, height lost); a reachable knot never moves; the feel floor (lfloor, default 0.15) bounds how short a nudged handle may get before amplitude gives. Replaces the fixed box. Check: a run of 100 mm strokes at 150 ms against 400 mm/s trims every top to 47 mm with the bottoms anchored at 0. Open: a through point trims toward the previous knot too, which lengthens the next piece; balancing it between its two pieces is the alternative if a script shows the need. Centering a trimmed stroke instead of anchoring it at the previous knot is the operator's call.
Window mock 2026-10-07: rail, window size and offset sliders rescale the script live; a rail strip shows the window band and the carriage; Play runs the render at real speed (Space). Found: angles must be held to the speed ceiling (a G0 chord or a G2 angle over vmax has no legal piece); a trimmed knot's hold moves with it so the hold stays flat; angles are re-solved from the trimmed chords (two rounds); a trim that reaches nothing legal still takes the least-over position. Three windows on the built-in script (100, 300, 500 mm) render inside the ceilings with 0, 9 and 13 trimmed knots.

title: Kinetic² never catches up on a dense stream once one knot is infeasible: a 60 Hz 1 Hz sine from rest crawls for 2 s at jmax 500
description: Found by the playground (kin-8ef). Knots p = 0.5 - 0.35 cos(2 pi t) at 60 Hz from rest at 0.15, defaults (vmax 3, amax 30, jmax 500, Blend floor 0.25). The cosine starts with a = 13.8 u/s^2, so the first knot cannot be met from rest under jmax (about 28 ms of ramp). Expected: a few tens of ms of lag, then tracking. Observed p every 250 ms: 0.150 0.158 0.176 0.201 0.222 0.263 0.296 0.325 0.378 (target 0.15 0.5 0.85 0.5 0.15 ...), the same authored ahead, streamed with KINETIC2_KNOT_SAMPLE (16 ms latency: ... 0.404), under Stretch, and on the previous kernel (not a regression). The same sine at 10 Hz tracks exactly (0.150 0.502 0.850 0.500 0.150 ...), and at jmax 5000 the 60 Hz one tracks. Reading: each later knot is judged from the lagging state and spent again (stretch shifts every later knot, Blend trims toward the previous end), so the lag compounds instead of closing. 60 Hz is the funscript scrub rate. Playground preset Scrub shows it.
notes:
2026-10-06: the crawl was the kernel's stream model, not the sine: with the stream replay (persisted samples, eased compression, min-jerk interior junctions, free tail velocity with a resting acceleration) the 60 Hz sine at jmax 500 should track after its infeasible first knots; re-measure with the real module and close if it does.
2026-10-06 re-measured with the stream model (bare kernel, 60 Hz 1 Hz sine of 0.35 from rest, streamed at 16 ms latency): jmax 500 still crawls (98 of 120 samples refused, peak speed 1.08 of 2.2); jmax 1000 and 5000 track with zero refusals. A piece's jerk at 60 Hz is about 300,000 times the mismatch between its mean speed and its end speeds, so a one-percent speed inconsistency saturates 5000 and a sixth of a percent saturates 500: the ceiling binds, not the model. The playground default is jmax 2000 and the README states the bound. Left open for the operator: document as the floor for 60 Hz streams, or lower the stream rate under 1000.
2026-10-06 later: re-placing a trailing sample's prior time by the replay rule (solver.hpp sampleTime) made the 60 Hz sine track at jmax 500 as well (0 refused, peak speed 2.396); the sticky stretched priors were the crawl. The ceiling ruling stands.
close_reason: Operator ruling 2026-10-06: not a defect. Ceilings are normalized (windows/s^3): 500 is 200,000 mm/s^3 on a 400 mm window, far below any real configuration; Nucleus's input default is 2,000,000 mm/s^3 (5000 normalized) and the machine tolerates 5,000,000. A 60 Hz stream needs about 1000 normalized (400,000 mm/s^3 on 400 mm) because a 17 ms quintic's jerk is ~300,000 x its speed mismatch. The playground default stays at 2000.

title: Kinetic² anomaly reporting: every re-solve re-reports each pending knot's spend; solver anomalies carry the knot's time, not the engine clock; ABI dropped flag is never observable
description: Found by the playground (kin-8ef). (1) solveWindow reports WaveformScaled/DeadlineStretched for every pending knot on every re-solve, so a streamed knot is reported once per submit while it is pending: 18 anomalies for 5 knots (starved stream), 830 for 60 (streamed scrub). types.hpp says 'one event per axis spent, so the counts read as a diagnosis'. (2) Anomaly::t_us is documented 'engine time at record', but solver kinds record the knot's solved time (e.g. 8304 ms = authored + the 8 s stretch cap, while the clock was at 200 ms); only SettleEngaged and KnotRefused carry the clock. (3) PlanFailed detail is the worst ceiling ratio (1e30 = kIllegal for no legal piece), not only the types.hpp sentinels. (4) ensureSolved erases dropped knots from the timeline and compacts sol[], so kinetic2_solved never returns dropped = 1; a reader can only learn of a drop from PlanFailed (target = authored p). The playground matches drops by that target.
notes:
2026-10-06: anomalies now report once per knot and kind (engine-side mask keyed by the knot's authored time). PlanFailed's detail is documented as a sentinel OR the last attempt's worst ratio. Anomaly t_us is the knot's time (documented). The dropped byte in the ABI stays 0 by construction: the engine erases dropped knots; the PlanFailed anomaly is the record.
kin-ys0: the 16-entry anomaly ring overflows when one solve reports a bundle: bench (D) solved 64 infeasible segments at once and only ~14 trims survived to popAnomaly. The solve budget now spreads a bundle over ticks, which hides it in the bench, but a single solve can still report more than 16.
